Triage: lands in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/` (the shipped `admin_full_access` / `organization_admin_no_bypass` bundles) ⇒ `domain:identity`. Type **Bug**. Escalated to `needs-user-decision`.

**Why escalated even though all four prisms agree.** This is on the human floor twice over: it is a **permission-boundary** change, and route (a) **removes a grant from a published capability** that every org admin holds today. Prism alignment is not a licence to take a floor decision — it only makes the sitting short.

The measurement quality is unusually high and worth trusting: the card does not merely observe an admin exporting, it *isolates the cause* — C1/C2/C3 show the gate enforcing, and the S1/S2/S2b table on a plain member proves the wildcard is honoured and that a per-object `false` already beats it. So "admin bypass" is disproven and "the shipped sets ship a wildcard export grant" is proven.

## Four-prism block

- **① Platform long-term coherence** — **(a)**. #5491 / PR #6684 already removed the `member_default` wildcard on the CRUD axes for this exact reason. The export axis keeping its wildcard is the leftover inconsistency, not a deliberate posture. (a) finishes a decision already taken; (b) adds a second mechanism to work around the first.
- **② Measured business pull** — **(a)**. A real app declares three objects exportable by nobody and the platform exports them anyway for any org admin, with no supported opt-out (`403 [not_overridable]` on the code-package metadata, and the org admin holds no app-authored set to put the `false` in). The pull is for the declaration to be true, not for a new authoring surface.
- **③ AI-agent error-resistance** — **(a)**. Today an app can declare "this object is exportable by nobody", ship, and be silently wrong. That is declared-≠-enforced on an export/exfiltration boundary — the worst axis for a silent gap. (b) leaves the wildcard in place and asks every app author to remember to counter it.
- **④ Startup scope discipline** — **(a)**. Removal, no new surface, no permanent obligation. (b) is a new authoring capability the platform would owe forever.

**All four → (a). Human floor ⇒ yours to rule.**

## Recommendation

**(a) — drop `allowExport` from the `'*'` entry of both shipped admin sets**, following #5491's precedent exactly.

The one question that makes this breaking, stated plainly so it is not discovered after the fact: **after (a), an org admin can no longer export anything they were not explicitly granted.** That is the intended effect, and it is a behaviour change for every existing install whose admins export today. Two sub-questions:
1. Should the platform sets instead ship explicit per-object export grants for the platform's own objects, so admin tooling keeps working?
2. Does this ride the current train, or does it want a breaking-change note and a release boundary? (`protocol:breaking` is not applied yet — say the word and this seat applies it.)

⛔ Note for whichever seat implements it: partial enforcement (fixing one of the two sets) is rejected on prism ③ — a half-closed export boundary reads as closed and is not.

Evidence: hotcrm#1152 probes `40-707.mjs`, `45-707-decisive2.mjs`, `46-707-sysadmin.mjs`.

**Maintainer ruling** (delegated adjudication; delegation 2026-08-15 verbatim 「决策你直接帮我做」, batch confirmed 「同意」): **direction (a) — remove `allowExport` from the `'*'` entry of both shipped admin sets** (`admin_full_access`, `organization_admin_no_bypass`).

This is the #5491 / PR #6684 precedent applied to the export axis: the CRUD wildcard was removed there deliberately; the export wildcard survived by omission, not by decision. After the change, an org admin exports exactly what app-authored sets grant — the card's own `system_admin`-set measurement shows that posture is already precise (declared-false ⇒ 403, declared-true ⇒ 200). An app declaring "exportable by nobody" becomes true for every principal.

Consequences handled, not hidden: this is a post-GA behaviour change for deployments whose admins relied on export-everything — breaking-class changeset (post-cut convention: `minor` + **BREAKING** + ADR-0087 disposition) with the migration prescription "grant `allowExport` explicitly in an app permission set where admin export is intended". Pins: the S2b specific-over-wildcard shape stays; the three formerly-leaking objects now 403 for the org owner; C1–C3 gate-enforcement controls preserved.

Rationale: 40-probe evidence shows the gate is exact for everyone else — the wildcard is the sole hole; declaration-is-enforcement matters most for AI-generated apps, which otherwise learn that export declarations are void for admins; removing a wildcard is a net shrink.

`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `domain:identity` seat dispatches (`security` retained).
